newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says Italy 97 budget unaffected by 96 deficit.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Italy 97 budget unaffected by 96 deficit.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said a larger-than-expected 1996 public sector deficit had no bearing on his government's 1997 budget.

"The fact that 1996 closed with a somewhat elevated deficit does not represent any prejudice regarding the effectiveness and seriousness of the (1997) budget," Prodi told reporters in his hometown of Bologna where he was spending the Epiphany holiday.

"I've already said clearly that our goal is to enter European monetary union and to clean up public finances," he said. "If a mini-budget in 1997 is necessary then we will do it, but for now we are monitoring the figures day by day to see what eventual remedies we might have to take."
The Treasury announced last Friday that Italy had run up a 1996 public sector deficit of 138.50 trillion lire ($90.5 million) -- well above a revised government target of 123 trillion lire.

Economists have said the 1996 deficit means Italy faces a monumental task in 1997 to bring its pubic finances in line and secure a place in European economic and monetary union (EMU) ahead of its launch in two years' time.
Parliament last month approved a 62.5 trillion lire deficit-cutting package for 1997.
